issuer: Florida Department of Revenue, Office of Technical Assistance
title: Florida DOR Technical Assistance Advisement 88C2-011: Property Subject to Tax - Shares of Co-op Apartment Association
subject: Property Subject to Tax - Shares of Co-op Apartment Association
text:
Dec 16, 1988
Re: Technical Assistance Advisement 88(C)2-011
Intangible Tax; Filing Requirements/Note Secured by
Cooperative Apartment Association Shares
Dear :
Thank you for your letter of October 12, 1988 requesting a
Declaratory Statement. From the information provided there is
insufficient information on which to issue a Declaratory
Statement. However, we are responding to your request as a
Technical Assistance Advisement.
Based on your letters of September 22, 1988 and October 12,
1988, the central question raised is whether shares in a
cooperative apartment association represent a class of real
property or intangible personal property. Cooperative apartment
houses are generally owned by several persons, usually as
stockholders in a corporation in which title is vested, or as
beneficiaries under a trust agreement, title being vested in the
trustee. The owners of the shares are given proprietary leases
of apartments in the cooperative apartment building.
As the name implies, a cooperative association or
corporation is an organization formed for the mutual benefit of
its members or for the prosecution of a common enterprise. Here
the common enterprise is the owning and maintaining of a
multiple unit apartment building, and the separate occupation of
the apartments by the members of the association. The ownership
of the apartment house and its maintenance is in common with the
other shareholders. Although each apartment occupant owns one or
more shares issued by the cooperative apartment building
association, such shares, through agreement between all
shareholders, is so tied in with the right to occupy an
apartment and the general operation, that the shares may not be
separated from the right of occupancy of the apartment.
In determining whether the shares are to be considered as

representing a class of real property or intangible personal
property, it must be determined what it is to the shareholder
owners. The shareholder owns a portion of the association. The
association is the owner of the apartment building (the real
property). The shareholder owns only the right to occupy a
specific apartment in the building, but only so long as the
shares are owned. The shares represent only the proprietary
right to occupy an apartment and ownership of the association.
This makes the shares in the association intangible personal
property as defined in s. 199.023(1), F.S.
The specific situation outlined in your letters shows that
your 42 1/2 shares in the cooperative association were sold to
XXX. For the purchase price of the shares XXX gave a note which
is secured by a lien on the cooperative apartment shares. The
note had an outstanding balance of $18,782.25 on January 1,
1988. This note, being secured by intangible personal property,
is subject only to the annual intangible tax imposed by s.
199.032, F.S.
As was stated in our letter of October 6, 1988, the
additional tax was billed due to a math error in the addition on
"Schedule A" of the 1988 intangible tax return. This resulted
in additional tax, after discount, of $9.60 plus interest of
$.13 for a total bill of $9.73.
This response constitutes a technical assistance advisement
under s. 213.22, F.S., which is binding on the Department only
under the facts and circumstances described in the request for
this advice as specified in s. 213.22, F.S. Our response is
predicated on those facts and the specific situation summarized
above. You are advised that subsequent statutory or
administrative rule changes or judicial interpretations of the
statutes or rules upon which this advice is based may subject
similar future transactions to a different treatment than
expressed in this response.
You are further advised that this response and your request
are public records under Chapter 119, F.S., which are subject to
disclosure to the public under the conditions of s. 213.22, F.S.
Your name, address, and any other details which might lead to

identification of the taxpayer must be deleted by the Department
before disclosure. In an effort to protect confidential
information, we request you notify the undersigned in writing
within 15 days of any deletions you wish made to the request or
this response.
Sincerely.
J.V. Parramore, Jr
Technical Assistant
Statutory Compliance Section
